title: Inference Metrics — TTFT, TPOT, ITL, Goodput, P99

questions.question: Which components dominate TTFT (time to first token)?
options: Queue time, network request time, and prefill time — TTFT = queue_time + network_request + prefill_time
Decode-only forward time, since TTFT is defined purely by the memory-bound decode step
Disk I/O for weights, since TTFT is dominated by reloading model weights from disk on every single request
Tokenizer GIL overhead, since TTFT is dominated by Python's tokenizer lock contention
questions.explanation: The lesson defines TTFT = queue_time + network_request + prefill_time, so all three of those components, not decode time, dominate it.

questions.question: Which metric does the lesson call the one that actually matters for product?
options: Aggregate throughput in tokens per second, since the lesson treats fleet-wide token volume as the product signal
Goodput — the fraction of requests meeting every SLO constraint (TTFT, TPOT, and E2E) simultaneously
GPU duty cycle, since the lesson treats hardware utilization as the proxy for whether users are served well
Mean ITL, since the lesson treats the average inter-token latency as the number reflecting user experience
questions.explanation: The lesson is explicit that throughput is a fleet-efficiency metric, but goodput -- the fraction of requests meeting every SLO constraint (TTFT, TPOT, and E2E) simultaneously -- is the one that reflects whether the product actually worked for users.

questions.question: Why is mean the wrong statistic to report for LLM latency?
options: Mean is never computable on streaming responses, since tokens arrive incrementally rather than as one batch
Mean only works for prefill latency, not decode latency, because decode is memory-bound rather than compute-bound
Mean is not supported by GenAI-Perf's ITL calculation, which only reports percentiles by design
LLM latency distributions are right-skewed; users routinely hit P99 outliers that mean hides
questions.explanation: The lesson's example shows mean TPOT of 9 ms hiding a P99 TPOT of 65 ms, because a right-skewed distribution (a few requests sharing a batch with a long-prefill neighbor) means users regularly hit the tail that the mean averages away.

questions.question: Why do GenAI-Perf and LLMPerf disagree on TPOT for the same run?
options: GenAI-Perf only runs on Blackwell GPUs, so its numbers are not comparable to LLMPerf runs on other hardware
LLMPerf uses microseconds and GenAI-Perf uses milliseconds, so the raw numbers differ by a unit conversion
GenAI-Perf excludes TTFT from the ITL calculation; LLMPerf includes it, so tool choice changes the number
They sample a different set of requests from the same run, so the percentile comparison is not apples-to-apples
questions.explanation: The lesson's worked example shows GenAI-Perf starting ITL from token 2 (excluding TTFT) while LLMPerf starts from token 1 (including TTFT), producing different numbers (7.07 ms vs 12.00 ms) for the identical run.

questions.question: For long-output requests (>500 tokens), which metric dominates end-to-end latency?
options: TTFT, the time to the first streamed token, which the lesson treats as dominant regardless of output length
TPOT times output length, since E2E = TTFT + TPOT * output_tokens + network_response and the TPOT term dominates
Cold-start time, since spinning up a fresh replica adds a fixed delay to every long-output request
Network response time, since transferring a long generated response back over the wire dominates total end-to-end latency
questions.explanation: E2E = TTFT + TPOT * output_tokens + network_response, and the lesson states that for long outputs (>500 tokens) E2E is TPOT-dominated -- TPOT times output length outweighs the fixed TTFT and network terms.

questions.question: Which set best captures the lesson's reasonable consumer-facing SLO for a 70B chat model in 2026?
options: P50 only, with no P90 or P99 reported, since the lesson treats the median as sufficient for consumer SLOs
TTFT P99 8s, TPOT P99 200ms, goodput 50% — thresholds far looser than what the lesson calls reasonable
TTFT P99 800 ms, TPOT P99 25 ms, E2E P99 3 s for <300-token outputs, goodput >= 99%
Mean TTFT 10 ms, mean TPOT 1 ms, with no percentile or goodput target specified at all
questions.explanation: The lesson gives exactly this SLO as the reasonable 2026 consumer-facing target: TTFT P99 <= 800 ms, TPOT P99 <= 25 ms, E2E P99 <= 3 s for <300-token outputs, and a goodput target >= 99%.
